5:36.en: Indeed, those who disbelieve - if they should have all that is in the earth and the like of it with it by which to ransom themselves from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, it will not be accepted from them, and for them is a painful punishment

5:37.ar: يُرِيدُونَ أَن يَخۡرُجُواْ مِنَ ٱلنَّارِ وَمَا هُم بِخَٰرِجِينَ مِنۡهَاۖ وَلَهُمۡ عَذَابࣱ مُّقِيمࣱ‏
5:37.en: They will wish to get out of the Fire, but never are they to emerge therefrom, and for them is an enduring punishment

5:38.ar: وَٱلسَّارِقُ وَٱلسَّارِقَةُ فَٱقۡطَعُوٓاْ أَيۡدِيَهُمَا جَزَآءَۢ بِمَا كَسَبَا نَكَٰلࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمࣱ‏
5:38.en: [As for] the thief, the male and the female, amputate their hands in recompense for what they committed as a deterrent [punishment] from Allah. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise

5:39.ar: فَمَن تَابَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ ظُلۡمِهِۦ وَأَصۡلَحَ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَتُوبُ عَلَيۡهِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمٌ
5:39.en: But whoever repents after his wrongdoing and reforms, indeed, Allah will turn to him in forgiveness. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful

5:40.ar: أَلَمۡ تَعۡلَمۡ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَهُۥ مُلۡكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ يُعَذِّبُ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَغۡفِرُ لِمَن يَشَآءُۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ‏
5:40.en: Do you not know that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth? He punishes whom He wills and forgives whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent

5:41.ar: ۞يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلرَّسُولُ لَا يَحۡزُنكَ ٱلَّذِينَ يُسَٰرِعُونَ فِي ٱلۡكُفۡرِ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوٓاْ ءَامَنَّا بِأَفۡوَٰهِهِمۡ وَلَمۡ تُؤۡمِن قُلُوبُهُمۡۛ وَمِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ هَادُواْۛ سَمَّٰعُونَ لِلۡكَذِبِ سَمَّٰعُونَ لِقَوۡمٍ ءَاخَرِينَ لَمۡ يَأۡتُوكَۖ يُحَرِّفُونَ ٱلۡكَلِمَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَوَاضِعِهِۦۖ يَقُولُونَ إِنۡ أُوتِيتُمۡ هَٰذَا فَخُذُوهُ وَإِن لَّمۡ تُؤۡتَوۡهُ فَٱحۡذَرُواْۚ وَمَن يُرِدِ ٱللَّهُ فِتۡنَتَهُۥ فَلَن تَمۡلِكَ لَهُۥ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ شَيۡـًٔاۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ لَمۡ يُرِدِ ٱللَّهُ أَن يُطَهِّرَ قُلُوبَهُمۡۚ لَهُمۡ فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَا خِزۡيࣱۖ وَلَهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمࣱ‏
5:41.en: O Messenger, let them not grieve you who hasten into disbelief of those who say, "We believe" with their mouths, but their hearts believe not, and from among the Jews. [They are] avid listeners to falsehood, listening to another people who have not come to you. They distort words beyond their [proper] usages, saying "If you are given this, take it; but if you are not given it, then beware." But he for whom Allah intends fitnah - never will you possess [power to do] for him a thing against Allah. Those are the ones for whom Allah does not intend to purify their hearts. For them in this world is disgrace, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment

ftC4BwltIcc.speaker: unsure
ftC4BwltIcc.speaker_note: host of the 2026 A Juz A Day series with no self-introduction here; same voice and format as the episode where the host gives another name
ftC4BwltIcc.title: A Juz A Day: 6th Juz - Fulfilling Our Commitments
ftC4BwltIcc.one_line: End of An-Nisa on injustice against the prophets and excess in religion, then Al-Ma'idah's theme of fulfilling commitments: rites, food, purification, justice, courage.
ftC4BwltIcc.summary: He finishes An-Nisa with the theme of injustice: sin is doubled when blame is pinned on the innocent, the wronged may speak out publicly yet pardoning is nobler, and the people of the book spoke unjustly about Musa, Maryam and Isa. Persistent injustice costs blessings, though the Quran never paints everyone with one brush. He stresses that Muslims alone hold that Isa was neither killed nor crucified but raised alive and will return, and notes the grammatical shift that singles out those who establish prayer. The prophets share one message, Musa is distinguished as the one Allah spoke to, and excess in religion means raising any prophet above servanthood, as the Trinity does. Al-Ma'idah's theme is fulfilling commitments, with its frequent address to believers. Its public covenants include the sanctity of the sacred months and offerings, lawful food with an exception for necessity, the food and chaste women of the people of the book (with caution about minority contexts), wudu and tayammum as purification rather than burden, and justice even toward those we hate. The Israelites who broke their pledges grew hard-hearted. The Prophet was told to pardon treachery despite holding power. The refusal to enter the holy land shows cowardice as a flaw of faith, and the two sons of Adam show envy and the sanctity of life.

outline.heading: Aim: understand the Quran in prayer without a translation
outline.gist: The series takes a big-picture view of each juz, hoping to inspire people to reach the point of understanding the recitation directly.

outline.heading: Repentance, and the doubled sin of blaming the innocent
outline.gist: Allah forgives those who seek forgiveness, but tawbah requires sincere resolve to stop; pinning one's sin on an innocent person adds slander to sin.

outline.heading: Injustice cast at the prophets; secret talk and opposing the Messenger
outline.gist: The verses prepare for the unjust statements made about prophets; no good in secret talk except charity, good and reconciliation.

outline.heading: The wronged may speak out, but pardon is nobler
outline.gist: Allah dislikes public evil speech except by one who was wronged; the right to justice remains, yet forgiving brings honour.

outline.heading: Demands for miracles and the calf
outline.gist: Asking for a book from the sky is a search for reasons not to believe; Musa's people even demanded to see Allah and later worshipped the calf.

outline.heading: Broken pledges, slander against Maryam and the claim to have killed Isa
outline.gist: Breaking pledges and killing prophets sealed hearts; the mocking claim to have killed the Messiah is false, and Allah raised him.

outline.heading: Isa's return; injustice costs blessings; not all are alike
outline.gist: All the people of the book will believe in Isa before his death; good things were forbidden for wrongdoing and usury, while those firm in knowledge believe.

outline.heading: Only Muslims say Isa did not die
outline.gist: Unlike Christians, Jews and secular historians, Muslims hold that he was raised alive; he cites a scriptural verse about angels bearing up the Messiah.

outline.heading: The grammatical shift that honours those who pray
outline.gist: In a list of believers' traits, those who establish prayer are set apart by a different grammatical form to stress how special they are.

outline.heading: The list of prophets, and Musa singled out
outline.gist: Revelation came to Nuh, Ibrahim and many others, most unnamed; Musa gets his own verse as the one Allah spoke to directly. Messengers leave mankind without excuse.

outline.heading: The final Messenger with the truth
outline.gist: Belief benefits the believer and disbelief harms only oneself; all prophets bring the same message and none should be spoken of unjustly.

outline.heading: Do not go to excess in religion: say not three
outline.gist: Isa was a messenger and a word from Allah; neither he nor the angels disdain servanthood.

outline.heading: Excess means raising a prophet above his rank
outline.gist: Divinity belongs to Allah alone; some Muslims also exaggerate the Prophet's status. He reasons with Christians that Allah having a son makes no sense.

outline.heading: An-Nisa closes with inheritance, full circle
outline.gist: The surah begins and ends with inheritance rules protecting the vulnerable, here the person with no parent or child.

outline.heading: Al-Ma'idah: the theme of fulfilling commitments
outline.gist: A theme is a track for study, not a container; the address to believers recurs far more often here than its share of the Quran.

outline.heading: Contracts are part of faith; the public covenants
outline.gist: Breaking one's word signals weak faith; the surah lists public obligations: the Ka'bah and Hajj rites, food, marriage, purification and standing for justice.

outline.heading: The sacred months, offerings and pilgrims
outline.gist: The one social contract pre-Islamic Arabs respected came from Ibrahim; Islam keeps its pure core and removes later accretions. Hunting resumes after the rites.

outline.heading: Do not let hatred push you to transgress
outline.gist: Anger at those who barred you from the Sacred Mosque must not lead to wrongdoing; cooperate in righteousness, not in sin.

outline.heading: What is forbidden to eat
outline.gist: What is haram is limited and everything else is halal: carrion, blood, pork, animals dedicated to others or killed violently without slaughter.

outline.heading: Religion perfected; necessity makes the forbidden permitted
outline.gist: Do not fear people when keeping these public covenants; one forced by hunger is forgiven.

outline.heading: Food of the people of the book: breaking bread
outline.gist: Shared food builds community with Jews and Christians based on shared values.

outline.heading: Marrying chaste women of the people of the book, with context
outline.gist: Permitted with all requirements, but revealed when Muslims held authority; in minority settings it needs case-by-case assessment for the children's faith.

outline.heading: Wudu, ghusl and tayammum
outline.gist: The Quran details purification while prayer's form comes from the Sunnah; ghusl for major impurity and clean earth when water is unavailable or harmful.

outline.heading: Purification is a blessing, not a burden
outline.gist: If the smallest ritual is not meant as hardship, neither is anything above it; paranoia about purity is a trap of Shaytan.

outline.heading: Stand firm for justice even toward those you hate
outline.gist: Remember the pledge 'we hear and obey'; bear witness impartially, because justice is closest to taqwa.

outline.heading: The twelve leaders and the broken pledge
outline.gist: Persistently breaking public covenants hardens hearts and leads to distorting and forgetting the revelation.

outline.heading: Pardon treachery and overlook it
outline.gist: As head of state with an army, the Prophet was told to pardon; power does not justify tyranny, and ignoring a troll can help them change.

outline.heading: The Christians' forgotten pledge and lasting enmity
outline.gist: Forgetting part of their covenant brought enmity among them, visible in centuries of sectarian violence.

outline.heading: Revelation as light; refuting divinity and 'chosen people'
outline.gist: Scripture makes things clear; no one could stop Allah if He chose to destroy the Messiah, and a chosen people would not be punished for their sins.

outline.heading: The refusal to enter the holy land: courage and cowardice
outline.gist: Two men urged entry, the people told Musa to go fight with his Lord; for breaking the pledge the land was withheld for forty years. Cowardice reflects a flaw in faith.

outline.heading: The two sons of Adam
outline.gist: Envy of the righteous brother led to the first murder; the raven showed how to bury him and the killer was left with regret.

outline.heading: Killing one soul is like killing all mankind
outline.gist: Life is sacred; the penal code and lawful war are narrow exceptions meant as deterrents.

outline.heading: Consoling the Messenger
outline.gist: The Prophet was hurt when called a liar; Allah consoles him that those who turn away are the problem.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Justice and refusing oppression
themes.note: Injustice against the innocent and against the prophets, the right of the wronged to speak, and justice even toward enemies.

themes.label: Oaths, promises, trust and loyalty
themes.note: Al-Ma'idah's theme: fulfilling the public covenants of faith; broken pledges harden hearts.

themes.label: Extremism, bad religiosity and distorted practice
themes.note: Excess in religion means attributing divinity or undue status to prophets.

themes.label: Stories of earlier prophets
themes.note: Isa raised alive and returning; the list of prophets and Musa's distinction.

themes.label: Jurisprudence rulings and how to approach fiqh
themes.note: Food, marriage to women of the book, and purification rules, framed as ease rather than burden.

themes.label: Mercy, forgiveness and pardoning people
themes.note: The Prophet told to pardon treachery while holding power.

themes.label: Courage and commitment
themes.note: Bravery is a tenet of faith and cowardice a sign of hypocrisy.

themes.label: Tolerance, pluralism and dealing with difference
themes.note: Shared food and cordial ties with the people of the book.

themes.label: The unlawfulness of harm and protecting others
themes.note: The first murder and the sanctity of every life.

maxims: Cowardice is a tenet of hypocrisy, bravery a tenet of faith
Having power does not mean becoming a tyrant
The Quran never paints everybody with one brush

stories.who: Musa's people refusing to enter the holy land
stories.point: Cowardice and broken pledges cost a blessing that was within reach.

stories.who: The two sons of Adam
stories.point: Envy leads to the gravest wrong; life is sacred.

stories.who: Isa raised alive
stories.point: He was not killed or crucified and will return.

contemporary: Marriage to women of the people of the book in Muslim-minority contexts
Christian sectarian violence in history
Exaggerating the Prophet's status among some Muslims today
takeaways: Keep every promise and contract as an act of faith
Never let anger at those who wronged you push you into injustice
Treat purification and worship as blessings, not sources of paranoia
Pardon and overlook rather than answering treachery in kind
Do not raise any prophet or person above servanthood to Allah

3:143.ar: وَلَقَدۡ كُنتُمۡ تَمَنَّوۡنَ ٱلۡمَوۡتَ مِن قَبۡلِ أَن تَلۡقَوۡهُ فَقَدۡ رَأَيۡتُمُوهُ وَأَنتُمۡ تَنظُرُونَ
3:143.en: And you had certainly wished for martyrdom before you encountered it, and you have [now] seen it [before you] while you were looking on

3:144.ar: وَمَا مُحَمَّدٌ إِلَّا رَسُولࣱ قَدۡ خَلَتۡ مِن قَبۡلِهِ ٱلرُّسُلُۚ أَفَإِيْن مَّاتَ أَوۡ قُتِلَ ٱنقَلَبۡتُمۡ عَلَىٰٓ أَعۡقَٰبِكُمۡۚ وَمَن يَنقَلِبۡ عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيۡهِ فَلَن يَضُرَّ ٱللَّهَ شَيۡـࣰٔ اۚ وَسَيَجۡزِي ٱللَّهُ ٱلشَّٰكِرِينَ
3:144.en: Muhammad is not but a messenger. [Other] messengers have passed on before him. So if he was to die or be killed, would you turn back on your heels [to unbelief]? And he who turns back on his heels will never harm Allah at all; but Allah will reward the grateful

3:145.ar: وَمَا كَانَ لِنَفۡسٍ أَن تَمُوتَ إِلَّا بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِ كِتَٰبࣰ ا مُّؤَجَّلࣰ اۗ وَمَن يُرِدۡ ثَوَابَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا نُؤۡتِهِۦ مِنۡهَا وَمَن يُرِدۡ ثَوَابَ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ نُؤۡتِهِۦ مِنۡهَاۚ وَسَنَجۡزِي ٱلشَّٰكِرِينَ
3:145.en: And it is not [possible] for one to die except by permission of Allah at a decree determined. And whoever desires the reward of this world - We will give him thereof; and whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter - We will give him thereof. And we will reward the grateful

3:154.ar: ثُمَّ أَنزَلَ عَلَيۡكُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ ٱلۡغَمِّ أَمَنَةࣰ نُّعَاسࣰ ا يَغۡشَىٰ طَآئِفَةࣰ مِّنكُمۡۖ وَطَآئِفَةࣱ قَدۡ أَهَمَّتۡهُمۡ أَنفُسُهُمۡ يَظُنُّونَ بِٱللَّهِ غَيۡرَ ٱلۡحَقِّ ظَنَّ ٱلۡجَٰهِلِيَّةِۖ يَقُولُونَ هَل لَّنَا مِنَ ٱلۡأَمۡرِ مِن شَيۡءࣲۗ قُلۡ إِنَّ ٱلۡأَمۡرَ كُلَّهُۥ لِلَّهِۗ يُخۡفُونَ فِيٓ أَنفُسِهِم مَّا لَا يُبۡدُونَ لَكَۖ يَقُولُونَ لَوۡ كَانَ لَنَا مِنَ ٱلۡأَمۡرِ شَيۡءࣱ مَّا قُتِلۡنَا هَٰهُنَاۗ قُل لَّوۡ كُنتُمۡ فِي بُيُوتِكُمۡ لَبَرَزَ ٱلَّذِينَ كُتِبَ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡقَتۡلُ إِلَىٰ مَضَاجِعِهِمۡۖ وَلِيَبۡتَلِيَ ٱللَّهُ مَا فِي صُدُورِكُمۡ وَلِيُمَحِّصَ مَا فِي قُلُوبِكُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمُۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ
3:154.en: Then after distress, He sent down upon you security [in the form of] drowsiness, overcoming a faction of you, while another faction worried about themselves, thinking of Allah other than the truth - the thought of ignorance, saying, "Is there anything for us [to have done] in this matter?" Say, "Indeed, the matter belongs completely to Allah." They conceal within themselves what they will not reveal to you. They say, "If there was anything we could have done in the matter, some of us would not have been killed right here." Say, "Even if you had been inside your houses, those decreed to be killed would have come out to their death beds." [It was] so that Allah might test what is in your breasts and purify what is in your hearts. And Allah is Knowing of that within the breasts

3:185.ar: كُلُّ نَفۡسࣲ ذَآئِقَةُ ٱلۡمَوۡتِۗ وَإِنَّمَا تُوَفَّوۡنَ أُجُورَكُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِۖ فَمَن زُحۡزِحَ عَنِ ٱلنَّارِ وَأُدۡخِلَ ٱلۡجَنَّةَ فَقَدۡ فَازَۗ وَمَا ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَآ إِلَّا مَتَٰعُ ٱلۡغُرُورِ
3:185.en: Every soul will taste death, and you will only be given your [full] compensation on the Day of Resurrection. So he who is drawn away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has attained [his desire]. And what is the life of this world except the enjoyment of delusion

4:41.ar: فَكَيۡفَ إِذَا جِئۡنَا مِن كُلِّ أُمَّةِۭ بِشَهِيدࣲ وَجِئۡنَا بِكَ عَلَىٰ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ شَهِيدࣰ ا
4:41.en: So how [will it be] when We bring from every nation a witness and we bring you, [O Muhammad] against these [people] as a witness

7:34.ar: وَلِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ أَجَلࣱۖ فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَجَلُهُمۡ لَا يَسۡتَأۡخِرُونَ سَاعَةࣰ وَلَا يَسۡتَقۡدِمُونَ
7:34.en: And for every nation is a [specified] term. So when their time has come, they will not remain behind an hour, nor will they precede [it]

21:34.ar: وَمَا جَعَلۡنَا لِبَشَرࣲ مِّن قَبۡلِكَ ٱلۡخُلۡدَۖ أَفَإِيْن مِّتَّ فَهُمُ ٱلۡخَٰلِدُونَ
21:34.en: And We did not grant to any man before you eternity [on earth]; so if you die - would they be eternal

hTmH_0H4oLE.speaker: adnan
hTmH_0H4oLE.speaker_note: Sheikh Adnan's Ramadan Quranic Themes series; speaks of his young son, hospital work and teaching Quran
hTmH_0H4oLE.title: Ramadan 2026, Night 4: Quranic Themes 2 - Accepting Mortality
hTmH_0H4oLE.one_line: Making peace with death through Uhud's lessons in Aal-Imran, 'every soul shall taste death', and the Prophet weeping at Ibn Mas'ud's recitation.
hTmH_0H4oLE.summary: He argues that even practising Muslims have lost a basic part of the faith: being at peace with the fact that life can end at any moment. Endings give life its meaning, so children should learn about death as soon as they can understand it, and they learn to take life for granted from parents who do; without this acceptance a loss becomes a breaking point rather than a lesson. Reading the Uhud verses, he shows companions who had wished for martyrdom faltering when a rumour spread that the Prophet had fallen. The Quran reminds them that Muhammad is a messenger like those before him, that faith cannot rest on any leader, teacher or hero, and that no soul dies except at its appointed time, which should produce courage rather than compromise. From 'every soul shall taste death' he urges people to cherish youth, health, company and Ramadan while they have them, to see worldly pleasures as short-lived highs, and to judge every pursuit by whether it moves them away from the Fire and into Paradise. He closes with the Prophet stopping Ibn Mas'ud's recitation in tears at the verse about bringing him as witness over his nation.

outline.heading: Accepting mortality: inner peace with an ending
outline.gist: Being at peace with not living forever is common to nearly all religions and fades as people drift from faith.

outline.heading: Practising Muslims have drifted from it too
outline.gist: Even people who read a lot of Quran and practise diligently have lost their acceptance that life can end at any moment.

outline.heading: The Quran's guidance assumes we are mortal
outline.gist: Every teaching in the Quran is built on the fact that people and nations pass; existence without an end would not be existence.

outline.heading: Endings give life meaning
outline.gist: A football game that never ended would mean nothing; purpose, meaning and morality exist because life ends.

outline.heading: Teaching children about death
outline.gist: Present death as early as children can grasp it, as with his four-year-old son, so they value being alive rather than to frighten them.

outline.heading: Children take life for granted when parents do
outline.gist: Children who take their blessings for granted learned that life is a given from parents who never feel they have enough.

outline.heading: Without acceptance, loss becomes a breaking point
outline.gist: An unexpected death breaks people's faith and sense of purpose instead of prompting reflection, which is why the Quran mentions death so often.

outline.heading: Aal-Imran and the shock of Uhud
outline.gist: The second half of the surah addresses internal threats to faith; Uhud shook the community and made some question the message.

outline.heading: You used to wish for death
outline.gist: Some had spoken eagerly of martyrdom; the Prophet taught never to wish to meet the enemy but to ask Allah for wellbeing and stand firm if it comes.

outline.heading: Seeing death changes everything
outline.gist: Intentions are easy in conversation; on the battlefield, seeing blood and hearing that the Prophet had fallen, perspective changed.

outline.heading: Mus'ab falls and the rumour spreads
outline.gist: Mus'ab ibn Umayr, who resembled the Prophet, was killed holding the banner, and the rumour of the Prophet's death caused chaos and flight.

outline.heading: Muhammad is only a messenger
outline.gist: Messengers passed before him; Allah never granted any human immortality, so would they turn on their heels if he died?

outline.heading: Islam is a gift; Allah rewards the grateful
outline.gist: Those who turn back harm only themselves; standing for something pure is a gift most people never receive.

outline.heading: No soul dies except at its appointed term
outline.gist: Your time was set before birth, which should comfort rather than fill you with regret; the term is hidden until it arrives.

outline.heading: Faith cannot rest on a leader
outline.gist: Your deen must stand on what you know to be true, whether or not the Prophet, your teacher, or political heroes remain.

outline.heading: When it's time, it's time
outline.gist: In hospital some who should have died live on and others fall without explanation; no doctor or technology can delay a decreed death.

outline.heading: Even at home, the decreed would meet their end
outline.gist: Knowing death cannot be outrun gives courage and inner peace, so a believer holds his ground instead of selling out his values.

outline.heading: Every soul shall taste death
outline.gist: The verse recited at every funeral states a fact decreed from the moment each soul was created.

outline.heading: Every organ has an expiry date
outline.gist: Even escaping all illness, the brain, eyes and every organ will eventually stop working.

outline.heading: Cherish youth and health while you have them
outline.gist: The body is a trust to care for; enjoy working joints and a quick memory now, because they decline.

outline.heading: You ain't dead yet
outline.gist: Every decade envies the one before; we are already tasting death, which should lift the mood because we are still alive.

outline.heading: Don't take life for granted
outline.gist: Enjoy every breath, the people around you and this blessed night; stepping back from taking life for granted makes everything under it precious.

outline.heading: Moved away from the Fire: the only victory
outline.gist: Full recompense comes on Judgment Day; whoever is edged away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has won.

outline.heading: 'It is only your deeds'
outline.gist: In a hadith qudsi Allah says He records people's deeds and returns them; whoever finds otherwise can blame only himself.

outline.heading: People and Ramadans: limited time only
outline.gist: Every person is interesting and precious, but our time with them and our Ramadans are limited, so enjoy them now.

outline.heading: Worldly life: short-lived highs
outline.gist: Worldly pleasures are illusions that seem bigger than they are, like the finest meal that sickens a full stomach.

outline.heading: Measure everything by the one win
outline.gist: Study, work and family should all move you toward Paradise; anything that does not deserves rethinking.

outline.heading: The Prophet asks Ibn Mas'ud to recite to him
outline.gist: For the first time the Prophet asked a companion, one of the greatest scholars of the Sahabah, to recite the Quran to him.

outline.heading: A student in the zone
outline.gist: Ibn Mas'ud recited close and fully absorbed, a state he describes from his own joy as a Quran teacher watching students recite.

outline.heading: 'Enough': a witness over his nation
outline.gist: At the verse about bringing a witness from every nation, the Prophet stopped him in tears, thinking of his own death and accounting.

themes.label: Mortality, death and preparing for it
themes.note: Accepting that life can end at any time is presented as essential to faith, courage, gratitude and purpose.

themes.label: Purpose, meaning and the point of life
themes.note: Meaning, purpose and morality exist because life ends.

themes.label: Parenting and raising children
themes.note: Teach children about death early and model not taking life for granted.

themes.label: Seerah events and their lessons
themes.note: Uhud and the rumour of the Prophet's death expose a weak acceptance of mortality among some companions.

themes.label: Eman: faith, certainty, doubt
themes.note: Faith must stand on conviction, not on the survival of any leader or teacher.

themes.label: Courage and commitment
themes.note: Knowing death is decreed removes the reason to flee or compromise.

themes.label: Gratitude (shukr) and appreciation
themes.note: Cherish youth, health, people and Ramadan rather than taking life for granted.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: The only victory is being moved from the Fire into Paradise, and each person receives his own deeds.

themes.label: Wealth, asceticism (zuhd), consumerism and money
themes.note: Worldly pleasures are short-lived highs that should not distract from the one real win.

themes.label: The Prophet's attributes, character and example
themes.note: The Prophet wept at the thought of standing as witness over his nation.

quran.point: Every nation has its appointed term
No human before the Prophet was granted immortality

hadith.gist: Do not wish to meet the enemy; ask Allah for wellbeing, and if you meet them, stand firm.
Hadith qudsi: it is only your deeds that I record for you and then repay; whoever finds good should praise Allah, and whoever finds otherwise should blame only himself.
The Prophet asked Ibn Mas'ud to recite to him and stopped him in tears at the verse about bringing a witness from every nation.

maxims: The beauty of it is that it ends
Life is not a given
When it's time, it's time
You ain't dead yet
Limited time only
There's no such thing as a win except that

stories.who: His four-year-old son
stories.point: Children need to meet the idea of death once they can grasp it, so they value life.

stories.who: Mus'ab ibn Umayr and the rumour at Uhud
stories.point: Faith that depends on one person collapses when that person seems to fall.

stories.who: Deaths seen in hospital
stories.point: Death follows its decreed time regardless of age or medicine.

stories.who: Ibn Mas'ud reciting to the Prophet
stories.point: Even the Prophet wept thinking of his death and the witness he would bear.

takeaways: Make peace with the fact that your life can end at any moment and let it sharpen your appreciation, not your gloom.
Model for your children that being alive is a blessing, not a given.
Ground your faith in conviction so it survives the loss of any leader, teacher or hero.
Cherish your youth, health, people and Ramadans while you have them.
Ask of every pursuit, from study to work, whether it moves you toward Paradise.

7:85.ar: وَإِلَىٰ مَدۡيَنَ أَخَاهُمۡ شُعَيۡبࣰ اۚ قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ ٱعۡبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنۡ إِلَٰهٍ غَيۡرُهُۥۖ قَدۡ جَآءَتۡكُم بَيِّنَةࣱ مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡۖ فَأَوۡفُواْ ٱلۡكَيۡلَ وَٱلۡمِيزَانَ وَلَا تَبۡخَسُواْ ٱلنَّاسَ أَشۡيَآءَهُمۡ وَلَا تُفۡسِدُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ بَعۡدَ إِصۡلَٰحِهَاۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ
7:85.en: And to [the people of] Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. There has come to you clear evidence from your Lord. So fulfill the measure and weight and do not deprive people of their due and cause not corruption upon the earth after its reformation. That is better for you, if you should be believers

7:86.ar: وَلَا تَقۡعُدُواْ بِكُلِّ صِرَٰطࣲ تُوعِدُونَ وَتَصُدُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ مَنۡ ءَامَنَ بِهِۦ وَتَبۡغُونَهَا عِوَجࣰ اۚ وَٱذۡكُرُوٓاْ إِذۡ كُنتُمۡ قَلِيلࣰ ا فَكَثَّرَكُمۡۖ وَٱنظُرُواْ كَيۡفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلۡمُفۡسِدِينَ
7:86.en: And do not sit on every path, threatening and averting from the way of Allah those who believe in Him, seeking to make it [seem] deviant. And remember when you were few and He increased you. And see how was the end of the corrupters

7:87.ar: وَإِن كَانَ طَآئِفَةࣱ مِّنكُمۡ ءَامَنُواْ بِٱلَّذِيٓ أُرۡسِلۡتُ بِهِۦ وَطَآئِفَةࣱ لَّمۡ يُؤۡمِنُواْ فَٱصۡبِرُواْ حَتَّىٰ يَحۡكُمَ ٱللَّهُ بَيۡنَنَاۚ وَهُوَ خَيۡرُ ٱلۡحَٰكِمِينَ
7:87.en: And if there should be a group among you who has believed in that with which I have been sent and a group that has not believed, then be patient until Allah judges between us. And He is the best of judges

7:88.ar: ۞قَالَ ٱلۡمَلَأُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ مِن قَوۡمِهِۦ لَنُخۡرِجَنَّكَ يَٰشُعَيۡبُ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مَعَكَ مِن قَرۡيَتِنَآ أَوۡ لَتَعُودُنَّ فِي مِلَّتِنَاۚ قَالَ أَوَلَوۡ كُنَّا كَٰرِهِينَ
7:88.en: Said the eminent ones who were arrogant among his people, "We will surely evict you, O Shu'ayb, and those who have believed with you from our city, or you must return to our religion." He said, "Even if we were unwilling

7:89.ar: قَدِ ٱفۡتَرَيۡنَا عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِبًا إِنۡ عُدۡنَا فِي مِلَّتِكُم بَعۡدَ إِذۡ نَجَّىٰنَا ٱللَّهُ مِنۡهَاۚ وَمَا يَكُونُ لَنَآ أَن نَّعُودَ فِيهَآ إِلَّآ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّنَاۚ وَسِعَ رَبُّنَا كُلَّ شَيۡءٍ عِلۡمًاۚ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ تَوَكَّلۡنَاۚ رَبَّنَا ٱفۡتَحۡ بَيۡنَنَا وَبَيۡنَ قَوۡمِنَا بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَأَنتَ خَيۡرُ ٱلۡفَٰتِحِينَ
7:89.en: We would have invented against Allah a lie if we returned to your religion after Allah had saved us from it. And it is not for us to return to it except that Allah, our Lord, should will. Our Lord has encompassed all things in knowledge. Upon Allah we have relied. Our Lord, decide between us and our people in truth, and You are the best of those who give decision

7:90.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلۡمَلَأُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِن قَوۡمِهِۦ لَئِنِ ٱتَّبَعۡتُمۡ شُعَيۡبًا إِنَّكُمۡ إِذࣰ ا لَّخَٰسِرُونَ
7:90.en: Said the eminent ones who disbelieved among his people, "If you should follow Shu'ayb, indeed, you would then be losers

7:91.ar: فَأَخَذَتۡهُمُ ٱلرَّجۡفَةُ فَأَصۡبَحُواْ فِي دَارِهِمۡ جَٰثِمِينَ
7:91.en: So the earthquake seized them, and they became within their home [corpses] fallen prone

7:92.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُواْ شُعَيۡبࣰ ا كَأَن لَّمۡ يَغۡنَوۡاْ فِيهَاۚ ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُواْ شُعَيۡبࣰ ا كَانُواْ هُمُ ٱلۡخَٰسِرِينَ
7:92.en: Those who denied Shu'ayb - it was as though they had never resided there. Those who denied Shu'ayb - it was they who were the losers

7:93.ar: فَتَوَلَّىٰ عَنۡهُمۡ وَقَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ لَقَدۡ أَبۡلَغۡتُكُمۡ رِسَٰلَٰتِ رَبِّي وَنَصَحۡتُ لَكُمۡۖ فَكَيۡفَ ءَاسَىٰ عَلَىٰ قَوۡمࣲ كَٰفِرِينَ
7:93.en: And he turned away from them and said, "O my people, I had certainly conveyed to you the messages of my Lord and advised you, so how could I grieve for a disbelieving people

7:94.ar: وَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا فِي قَرۡيَةࣲ مِّن نَّبِيٍّ إِلَّآ أَخَذۡنَآ أَهۡلَهَا بِٱلۡبَأۡسَآءِ وَٱلضَّرَّآءِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَضَّرَّعُونَ
7:94.en: And We sent to no city a prophet [who was denied] except that We seized its people with poverty and hardship that they might humble themselves [to Allah]

7:95.ar: ثُمَّ بَدَّلۡنَا مَكَانَ ٱلسَّيِّئَةِ ٱلۡحَسَنَةَ حَتَّىٰ عَفَواْ وَّقَالُواْ قَدۡ مَسَّ ءَابَآءَنَا ٱلضَّرَّآءُ وَٱلسَّرَّآءُ فَأَخَذۡنَٰهُم بَغۡتَةࣰ وَهُمۡ لَا يَشۡعُرُونَ
7:95.en: Then We exchanged in place of the bad [condition], good, until they increased [and prospered] and said, "Our fathers [also] were touched with hardship and ease." So We seized them suddenly while they did not perceive

7:96.ar: وَلَوۡ أَنَّ أَهۡلَ ٱلۡقُرَىٰٓ ءَامَنُواْ وَٱتَّقَوۡاْ لَفَتَحۡنَا عَلَيۡهِم بَرَكَٰتࣲ مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَٰكِن كَذَّبُواْ فَأَخَذۡنَٰهُم بِمَا كَانُواْ يَكۡسِبُونَ
7:96.en: And if only the people of the cities had believed and feared Allah, We would have opened upon them blessings from the heaven and the earth; but they denied [the messengers], so We seized them for what they were earning

7:97.ar: أَفَأَمِنَ أَهۡلُ ٱلۡقُرَىٰٓ أَن يَأۡتِيَهُم بَأۡسُنَا بَيَٰتࣰ ا وَهُمۡ نَآئِمُونَ
7:97.en: Then, did the people of the cities feel secure from Our punishment coming to them at night while they were asleep

7:98.ar: أَوَأَمِنَ أَهۡلُ ٱلۡقُرَىٰٓ أَن يَأۡتِيَهُم بَأۡسُنَا ضُحࣰ ى وَهُمۡ يَلۡعَبُونَ
7:98.en: Or did the people of the cities feel secure from Our punishment coming to them in the morning while they were at play

7:99.ar: أَفَأَمِنُواْ مَكۡرَ ٱللَّهِۚ فَلَا يَأۡمَنُ مَكۡرَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلۡقَوۡمُ ٱلۡخَٰسِرُونَ
7:99.en: Then did they feel secure from the plan of Allah? But no one feels secure from the plan of Allah except the losing people

7:100.ar: أَوَلَمۡ يَهۡدِ لِلَّذِينَ يَرِثُونَ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ أَهۡلِهَآ أَن لَّوۡ نَشَآءُ أَصَبۡنَٰهُم بِذُنُوبِهِمۡۚ وَنَطۡبَعُ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمۡ فَهُمۡ لَا يَسۡمَعُونَ
7:100.en: Has it not become clear to those who inherited the earth after its [previous] people that if We willed, We could afflict them for their sins? But We seal over their hearts so they do not hear

7:101.ar: تِلۡكَ ٱلۡقُرَىٰ نَقُصُّ عَلَيۡكَ مِنۡ أَنۢبَآئِهَاۚ وَلَقَدۡ جَآءَتۡهُمۡ رُسُلُهُم بِٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتِ فَمَا كَانُواْ لِيُؤۡمِنُواْ بِمَا كَذَّبُواْ مِن قَبۡلُۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يَطۡبَعُ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
7:101.en: Those cities - We relate to you, [O Muhammad], some of their news. And certainly did their messengers come to them with clear proofs, but they were not to believe in that which they had denied before. Thus does Allah seal over the hearts of the disbelievers

7:102.ar: وَمَا وَجَدۡنَا لِأَكۡثَرِهِم مِّنۡ عَهۡدࣲۖ وَإِن وَجَدۡنَآ أَكۡثَرَهُمۡ لَفَٰسِقِينَ
7:102.en: And We did not find for most of them any covenant; but indeed, We found most of them defiantly disobedient

7:103.ar: ثُمَّ بَعَثۡنَا مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِم مُّوسَىٰ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ إِلَىٰ فِرۡعَوۡنَ وَمَلَإِيْهِۦ فَظَلَمُواْ بِهَاۖ فَٱنظُرۡ كَيۡفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلۡمُفۡسِدِينَ
7:103.en: Then We sent after them Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his establishment, but they were unjust toward them. So see how was the end of the corrupters

7:104.ar: وَقَالَ مُوسَىٰ يَٰفِرۡعَوۡنُ إِنِّي رَسُولࣱ مِّن رَّبِّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
7:104.en: And Moses said, "O Pharaoh, I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds

7:105.ar: حَقِيقٌ عَلَىٰٓ أَن لَّآ أَقُولَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلۡحَقَّۚ قَدۡ جِئۡتُكُم بِبَيِّنَةࣲ مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡ فَأَرۡسِلۡ مَعِيَ بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ
7:105.en: [Who is] obligated not to say about Allah except the truth. I have come to you with clear evidence from your Lord, so send with me the Children of Israel

7:106.ar: قَالَ إِن كُنتَ جِئۡتَ بِـَٔايَةࣲ فَأۡتِ بِهَآ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ
7:106.en: [Pharaoh] said, "If you have come with a sign, then bring it forth, if you should be of the truthful

7:107.ar: فَأَلۡقَىٰ عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِيَ ثُعۡبَانࣱ مُّبِينࣱ‏
7:107.en: So Moses threw his staff, and suddenly it was a serpent, manifest

7:108.ar: وَنَزَعَ يَدَهُۥ فَإِذَا هِيَ بَيۡضَآءُ لِلنَّٰظِرِينَ
7:108.en: And he drew out his hand; thereupon it was white [with radiance] for the observers

7:109.ar: قَالَ ٱلۡمَلَأُ مِن قَوۡمِ فِرۡعَوۡنَ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَسَٰحِرٌ عَلِيمࣱ‏
7:109.en: Said the eminent among the people of Pharaoh, "Indeed, this is a learned magician

7:110.ar: يُرِيدُ أَن يُخۡرِجَكُم مِّنۡ أَرۡضِكُمۡۖ فَمَاذَا تَأۡمُرُونَ
7:110.en: Who wants to expel you from your land [through magic], so what do you instruct

7:111.ar: قَالُوٓاْ أَرۡجِهۡ وَأَخَاهُ وَأَرۡسِلۡ فِي ٱلۡمَدَآئِنِ حَٰشِرِينَ
7:111.en: They said, "Postpone [the matter of] him and his brother and send among the cities gatherers

7:112.en: Who will bring you every learned magician

7:113.ar: وَجَآءَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ فِرۡعَوۡنَ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّ لَنَا لَأَجۡرًا إِن كُنَّا نَحۡنُ ٱلۡغَٰلِبِينَ
7:113.en: And the magicians came to Pharaoh. They said, "Indeed for us is a reward if we are the predominant

7:114.en: He said, "Yes, and, [moreover], you will be among those made near [to me]

7:115.ar: قَالُواْ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِمَّآ أَن تُلۡقِيَ وَإِمَّآ أَن نَّكُونَ نَحۡنُ ٱلۡمُلۡقِينَ
7:115.en: They said, "O Moses, either you throw [your staff], or we will be the ones to throw [first]

7:116.ar: قَالَ أَلۡقُواْۖ فَلَمَّآ أَلۡقَوۡاْ سَحَرُوٓاْ أَعۡيُنَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَٱسۡتَرۡهَبُوهُمۡ وَجَآءُو بِسِحۡرٍ عَظِيمࣲ‏
7:116.en: He said, "Throw," and when they threw, they bewitched the eyes of the people and struck terror into them, and they presented a great [feat of] magic

7:117.ar: ۞وَأَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنۡ أَلۡقِ عَصَاكَۖ فَإِذَا هِيَ تَلۡقَفُ مَا يَأۡفِكُونَ
7:117.en: And We inspired to Moses, "Throw your staff," and at once it devoured what they were falsifying

7:118.ar: فَوَقَعَ ٱلۡحَقُّ وَبَطَلَ مَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
7:118.en: So the truth was established, and abolished was what they were doing

7:119.en: And Pharaoh and his people were overcome right there and became debased

7:120.en: And the magicians fell down in prostration [to Allah]

7:121.en: They said, "We have believed in the Lord of the worlds

7:122.en: The Lord of Moses and Aaron

7:123.ar: قَالَ فِرۡعَوۡنُ ءَامَنتُم بِهِۦ قَبۡلَ أَنۡ ءَاذَنَ لَكُمۡۖ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَمَكۡرࣱ مَّكَرۡتُمُوهُ فِي ٱلۡمَدِينَةِ لِتُخۡرِجُواْ مِنۡهَآ أَهۡلَهَاۖ فَسَوۡفَ تَعۡلَمُونَ
7:123.en: Said Pharaoh, "You believed in him before I gave you permission. Indeed, this is a conspiracy which you conspired in the city to expel therefrom its people. But you are going to know

7:124.ar: لَأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيۡدِيَكُمۡ وَأَرۡجُلَكُم مِّنۡ خِلَٰفࣲ ثُمَّ لَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمۡ أَجۡمَعِينَ
7:124.en: I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides; then I will surely crucify you all

7:125.en: They said, "Indeed, to our Lord we will return

7:126.ar: وَمَا تَنقِمُ مِنَّآ إِلَّآ أَنۡ ءَامَنَّا بِـَٔايَٰتِ رَبِّنَا لَمَّا جَآءَتۡنَاۚ رَبَّنَآ أَفۡرِغۡ عَلَيۡنَا صَبۡرࣰ ا وَتَوَفَّنَا مُسۡلِمِينَ
7:126.en: And you do not resent us except because we believed in the signs of our Lord when they came to us. Our Lord, pour upon us patience and let us die as Muslims [in submission to You]

7:127.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلۡمَلَأُ مِن قَوۡمِ فِرۡعَوۡنَ أَتَذَرُ مُوسَىٰ وَقَوۡمَهُۥ لِيُفۡسِدُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَيَذَرَكَ وَءَالِهَتَكَۚ قَالَ سَنُقَتِّلُ أَبۡنَآءَهُمۡ وَنَسۡتَحۡيِۦ نِسَآءَهُمۡ وَإِنَّا فَوۡقَهُمۡ قَٰهِرُونَ
7:127.en: And the eminent among the people of Pharaoh said," Will you leave Moses and his people to cause corruption in the land and abandon you and your gods?" [Pharaoh] said, "We will kill their sons and keep their women alive; and indeed, we are subjugators over them

7:128.ar: قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوۡمِهِ ٱسۡتَعِينُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱصۡبِرُوٓاْۖ إِنَّ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ لِلَّهِ يُورِثُهَا مَن يَشَآءُ مِنۡ عِبَادِهِۦۖ وَٱلۡعَٰقِبَةُ لِلۡمُتَّقِينَ
7:128.en: Said Moses to his people, "Seek help through Allah and be patient. Indeed, the earth belongs to Allah. He causes to inherit it whom He wills of His servants. And the [best] outcome is for the righteous

7:129.ar: قَالُوٓاْ أُوذِينَا مِن قَبۡلِ أَن تَأۡتِيَنَا وَمِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا جِئۡتَنَاۚ قَالَ عَسَىٰ رَبُّكُمۡ أَن يُهۡلِكَ عَدُوَّكُمۡ وَيَسۡتَخۡلِفَكُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَيَنظُرَ كَيۡفَ تَعۡمَلُونَ
7:129.en: They said, "We have been harmed before you came to us and after you have come to us." He said, "Perhaps your Lord will destroy your enemy and grant you succession in the land and see how you will do

7:130.ar: وَلَقَدۡ أَخَذۡنَآ ءَالَ فِرۡعَوۡنَ بِٱلسِّنِينَ وَنَقۡصࣲ مِّنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَذَّكَّرُونَ
7:130.en: And We certainly seized the people of Pharaoh with years of famine and a deficiency in fruits that perhaps they would be reminded

7:131.ar: فَإِذَا جَآءَتۡهُمُ ٱلۡحَسَنَةُ قَالُواْ لَنَا هَٰذِهِۦۖ وَإِن تُصِبۡهُمۡ سَيِّئَةࣱ يَطَّيَّرُواْ بِمُوسَىٰ وَمَن مَّعَهُۥٓۗ أَلَآ إِنَّمَا طَٰٓئِرُهُمۡ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَهُمۡ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
7:131.en: But when good came to them, they said, "This is ours [by right]." And if a bad [condition] struck them, they saw an evil omen in Moses and those with him. Unquestionably, their fortune is with Allah, but most of them do not know

7:132.ar: وَقَالُواْ مَهۡمَا تَأۡتِنَا بِهِۦ مِنۡ ءَايَةࣲ لِّتَسۡحَرَنَا بِهَا فَمَا نَحۡنُ لَكَ بِمُؤۡمِنِينَ
7:132.en: And they said, "No matter what sign you bring us with which to bewitch us, we will not be believers in you

7:133.ar: فَأَرۡسَلۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلطُّوفَانَ وَٱلۡجَرَادَ وَٱلۡقُمَّلَ وَٱلضَّفَادِعَ وَٱلدَّمَ ءَايَٰتࣲ مُّفَصَّلَٰتࣲ فَٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ وَكَانُواْ قَوۡمࣰ ا مُّجۡرِمِينَ
7:133.en: So We sent upon them the flood and locusts and lice and frogs and blood as distinct signs, but they were arrogant and were a criminal people

7:134.ar: وَلَمَّا وَقَعَ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلرِّجۡزُ قَالُواْ يَٰمُوسَى ٱدۡعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ بِمَا عَهِدَ عِندَكَۖ لَئِن كَشَفۡتَ عَنَّا ٱلرِّجۡزَ لَنُؤۡمِنَنَّ لَكَ وَلَنُرۡسِلَنَّ مَعَكَ بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ
7:134.en: And when the punishment descended upon them, they said, "O Moses, invoke for us your Lord by what He has promised you. If you [can] remove the punishment from us, we will surely believe you, and we will send with you the Children of Israel

7:135.ar: فَلَمَّا كَشَفۡنَا عَنۡهُمُ ٱلرِّجۡزَ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍ هُم بَٰلِغُوهُ إِذَا هُمۡ يَنكُثُونَ
7:135.en: But when We removed the punishment from them until a term which they were to reach, then at once they broke their word

7:136.ar: فَٱنتَقَمۡنَا مِنۡهُمۡ فَأَغۡرَقۡنَٰهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡيَمِّ بِأَنَّهُمۡ كَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا وَكَانُواْ عَنۡهَا غَٰفِلِينَ
7:136.en: So We took retribution from them, and We drowned them in the sea because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them

7:137.ar: وَأَوۡرَثۡنَا ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَانُواْ يُسۡتَضۡعَفُونَ مَشَٰرِقَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَغَٰرِبَهَا ٱلَّتِي بَٰرَكۡنَا فِيهَاۖ وَتَمَّتۡ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ ٱلۡحُسۡنَىٰ عَلَىٰ بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ بِمَا صَبَرُواْۖ وَدَمَّرۡنَا مَا كَانَ يَصۡنَعُ فِرۡعَوۡنُ وَقَوۡمُهُۥ وَمَا كَانُواْ يَعۡرِشُونَ
7:137.en: And We caused the people who had been oppressed to inherit the eastern regions of the land and the western ones, which We had blessed. And the good word of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel because of what they had patiently endured. And We destroyed [all] that Pharaoh and his people were producing and what they had been building

7:138.ar: وَجَٰوَزۡنَا بِبَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱلۡبَحۡرَ فَأَتَوۡاْ عَلَىٰ قَوۡمࣲ يَعۡكُفُونَ عَلَىٰٓ أَصۡنَامࣲ لَّهُمۡۚ قَالُواْ يَٰمُوسَى ٱجۡعَل لَّنَآ إِلَٰهࣰ ا كَمَا لَهُمۡ ءَالِهَةࣱۚ قَالَ إِنَّكُمۡ قَوۡمࣱ تَجۡهَلُونَ
7:138.en: And We took the Children of Israel across the sea; then they came upon a people intent in devotion to [some] idols of theirs. They said, "O Moses, make for us a god just as they have gods." He said, "Indeed, you are a people behaving ignorantly

7:139.ar: إِنَّ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ مُتَبَّرࣱ مَّا هُمۡ فِيهِ وَبَٰطِلࣱ مَّا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
7:139.en: Indeed, those [worshippers] - destroyed is that in which they are [engaged], and worthless is whatever they were doing

7:140.ar: قَالَ أَغَيۡرَ ٱللَّهِ أَبۡغِيكُمۡ إِلَٰهࣰ ا وَهُوَ فَضَّلَكُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
7:140.en: He said, "Is it other than Allah I should desire for you as a god while He has preferred you over the worlds

7:141.ar: وَإِذۡ أَنجَيۡنَٰكُم مِّنۡ ءَالِ فِرۡعَوۡنَ يَسُومُونَكُمۡ سُوٓءَ ٱلۡعَذَابِ يُقَتِّلُونَ أَبۡنَآءَكُمۡ وَيَسۡتَحۡيُونَ نِسَآءَكُمۡۚ وَفِي ذَٰلِكُم بَلَآءࣱ مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡ عَظِيمࣱ‏
7:141.en: And [recall, O Children of Israel], when We saved you from the people of Pharaoh, [who were] afflicting you with the worst torment - killing your sons and keeping your women alive. And in that was a great trial from your Lord

7:142.ar: ۞وَوَٰعَدۡنَا مُوسَىٰ ثَلَٰثِينَ لَيۡلَةࣰ وَأَتۡمَمۡنَٰهَا بِعَشۡرࣲ فَتَمَّ مِيقَٰتُ رَبِّهِۦٓ أَرۡبَعِينَ لَيۡلَةࣰۚ وَقَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِأَخِيهِ هَٰرُونَ ٱخۡلُفۡنِي فِي قَوۡمِي وَأَصۡلِحۡ وَلَا تَتَّبِعۡ سَبِيلَ ٱلۡمُفۡسِدِينَ
7:142.en: And We made an appointment with Moses for thirty nights and perfected them by [the addition of] ten; so the term of his Lord was completed as forty nights. And Moses said to his brother Aaron, "Take my place among my people, do right [by them], and do not follow the way of the corrupters

7:143.ar: وَلَمَّا جَآءَ مُوسَىٰ لِمِيقَٰتِنَا وَكَلَّمَهُۥ رَبُّهُۥ قَالَ رَبِّ أَرِنِيٓ أَنظُرۡ إِلَيۡكَۚ قَالَ لَن تَرَىٰنِي وَلَٰكِنِ ٱنظُرۡ إِلَى ٱلۡجَبَلِ فَإِنِ ٱسۡتَقَرَّ مَكَانَهُۥ فَسَوۡفَ تَرَىٰنِيۚ فَلَمَّا تَجَلَّىٰ رَبُّهُۥ لِلۡجَبَلِ جَعَلَهُۥ دَكࣰّ ا وَخَرَّ مُوسَىٰ صَعِقࣰ اۚ فَلَمَّآ أَفَاقَ قَالَ سُبۡحَٰنَكَ تُبۡتُ إِلَيۡكَ وَأَنَا۠ أَوَّلُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
7:143.en: And when Moses arrived at Our appointed time and his Lord spoke to him, he said, "My Lord, show me [Yourself] that I may look at You." [Allah] said, "You will not see Me, but look at the mountain; if it should remain in place, then you will see Me." But when his Lord appeared to the mountain, He rendered it level, and Moses fell unconscious. And when he awoke, he said, "Exalted are You! I have repented to You, and I am the first of the believers

7:144.ar: قَالَ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنِّي ٱصۡطَفَيۡتُكَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ بِرِسَٰلَٰتِي وَبِكَلَٰمِي فَخُذۡ مَآ ءَاتَيۡتُكَ وَكُن مِّنَ ٱلشَّٰكِرِينَ
7:144.en: [Allah] said, "O Moses, I have chosen you over the people with My messages and My words [to you]. So take what I have given you and be among the grateful

7:145.ar: وَكَتَبۡنَا لَهُۥ فِي ٱلۡأَلۡوَاحِ مِن كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ مَّوۡعِظَةࣰ وَتَفۡصِيلࣰ ا لِّكُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ فَخُذۡهَا بِقُوَّةࣲ وَأۡمُرۡ قَوۡمَكَ يَأۡخُذُواْ بِأَحۡسَنِهَاۚ سَأُوْرِيكُمۡ دَارَ ٱلۡفَٰسِقِينَ
7:145.en: And We wrote for him on the tablets [something] of all things - instruction and explanation for all things, [saying], "Take them with determination and order your people to take the best of it. I will show you the home of the defiantly disobedient

7:65.ar: ۞وَإِلَىٰ عَادٍ أَخَاهُمۡ هُودࣰ اۚ قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ ٱعۡبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنۡ إِلَٰهٍ غَيۡرُهُۥٓۚ أَفَلَا تَتَّقُونَ
7:65.en: And to the 'Aad [We sent] their brother Hud. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. Then will you not fear Him

7:73.ar: وَإِلَىٰ ثَمُودَ أَخَاهُمۡ صَٰلِحࣰ اۚ قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ ٱعۡبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنۡ إِلَٰهٍ غَيۡرُهُۥۖ قَدۡ جَآءَتۡكُم بَيِّنَةࣱ مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡۖ هَٰذِهِۦ نَاقَةُ ٱللَّهِ لَكُمۡ ءَايَةࣰۖ فَذَرُوهَا تَأۡكُلۡ فِيٓ أَرۡضِ ٱللَّهِۖ وَلَا تَمَسُّوهَا بِسُوٓءࣲ فَيَأۡخُذَكُمۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمࣱ‏
7:73.en: And to the Thamud [We sent] their brother Salih. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. There has come to you clear evidence from your Lord. This is the she-camel of Allah [sent] to you as a sign. So leave her to eat within Allah 's land and do not touch her with harm, lest there seize you a painful punishment

7:148.ar: وَٱتَّخَذَ قَوۡمُ مُوسَىٰ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦ مِنۡ حُلِيِّهِمۡ عِجۡلࣰ ا جَسَدࣰ ا لَّهُۥ خُوَارٌۚ أَلَمۡ يَرَوۡاْ أَنَّهُۥ لَا يُكَلِّمُهُمۡ وَلَا يَهۡدِيهِمۡ سَبِيلًاۘ ٱتَّخَذُوهُ وَكَانُواْ ظَٰلِمِينَ
7:148.en: And the people of Moses made, after [his departure], from their ornaments a calf - an image having a lowing sound. Did they not see that it could neither speak to them nor guide them to a way? They took it [for worship], and they were wrongdoers

7:149.ar: وَلَمَّا سُقِطَ فِيٓ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَرَأَوۡاْ أَنَّهُمۡ قَدۡ ضَلُّواْ قَالُواْ لَئِن لَّمۡ يَرۡحَمۡنَا رَبُّنَا وَيَغۡفِرۡ لَنَا لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلۡخَٰسِرِينَ
7:149.en: And when regret overcame them and they saw that they had gone astray, they said, "If our Lord does not have mercy upon us and forgive us, we will surely be among the losers

7:150.ar: وَلَمَّا رَجَعَ مُوسَىٰٓ إِلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِۦ غَضۡبَٰنَ أَسِفࣰ ا قَالَ بِئۡسَمَا خَلَفۡتُمُونِي مِنۢ بَعۡدِيٓۖ أَعَجِلۡتُمۡ أَمۡرَ رَبِّكُمۡۖ وَأَلۡقَى ٱلۡأَلۡوَاحَ وَأَخَذَ بِرَأۡسِ أَخِيهِ يَجُرُّهُۥٓ إِلَيۡهِۚ قَالَ ٱبۡنَ أُمَّ إِنَّ ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱسۡتَضۡعَفُونِي وَكَادُواْ يَقۡتُلُونَنِي فَلَا تُشۡمِتۡ بِيَ ٱلۡأَعۡدَآءَ وَلَا تَجۡعَلۡنِي مَعَ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
7:150.en: And when Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved, he said, "How wretched is that by which you have replaced me after [my departure]. Were you impatient over the matter of your Lord?" And he threw down the tablets and seized his brother by [the hair of] his head, pulling him toward him. [Aaron] said, "O son of my mother, indeed the people oppressed me and were about to kill me, so let not the enemies rejoice over me and do not place me among the wrongdoing people

7:151.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ ٱغۡفِرۡ لِي وَلِأَخِي وَأَدۡخِلۡنَا فِي رَحۡمَتِكَۖ وَأَنتَ أَرۡحَمُ ٱلرَّٰحِمِينَ
7:151.en: [Moses] said, "My Lord, forgive me and my brother and admit us into Your mercy, for You are the most merciful of the merciful

7:152.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُواْ ٱلۡعِجۡلَ سَيَنَالُهُمۡ غَضَبࣱ مِّن رَّبِّهِمۡ وَذِلَّةࣱ فِي ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَاۚ وَكَذَٰلِكَ نَجۡزِي ٱلۡمُفۡتَرِينَ
7:152.en: Indeed, those who took the calf [for worship] will obtain anger from their Lord and humiliation in the life of this world, and thus do We recompense the inventors [of falsehood]

7:153.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ عَمِلُواْ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ ثُمَّ تَابُواْ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهَا وَءَامَنُوٓاْ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهَا لَغَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
7:153.en: But those who committed misdeeds and then repented after them and believed - indeed your Lord, thereafter, is Forgiving and Merciful

7:154.ar: وَلَمَّا سَكَتَ عَن مُّوسَى ٱلۡغَضَبُ أَخَذَ ٱلۡأَلۡوَاحَۖ وَفِي نُسۡخَتِهَا هُدࣰ ى وَرَحۡمَةࣱ لِّلَّذِينَ هُمۡ لِرَبِّهِمۡ يَرۡهَبُونَ
7:154.en: And when the anger subsided in Moses, he took up the tablets; and in their inscription was guidance and mercy for those who are fearful of their Lord

7:155.ar: وَٱخۡتَارَ مُوسَىٰ قَوۡمَهُۥ سَبۡعِينَ رَجُلࣰ ا لِّمِيقَٰتِنَاۖ فَلَمَّآ أَخَذَتۡهُمُ ٱلرَّجۡفَةُ قَالَ رَبِّ لَوۡ شِئۡتَ أَهۡلَكۡتَهُم مِّن قَبۡلُ وَإِيَّٰيَۖ أَتُهۡلِكُنَا بِمَا فَعَلَ ٱلسُّفَهَآءُ مِنَّآۖ إِنۡ هِيَ إِلَّا فِتۡنَتُكَ تُضِلُّ بِهَا مَن تَشَآءُ وَتَهۡدِي مَن تَشَآءُۖ أَنتَ وَلِيُّنَا فَٱغۡفِرۡ لَنَا وَٱرۡحَمۡنَاۖ وَأَنتَ خَيۡرُ ٱلۡغَٰفِرِينَ
7:155.en: And Moses chose from his people seventy men for Our appointment. And when the earthquake seized them, he said, "My Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them before and me [as well]. Would You destroy us for what the foolish among us have done? This is not but Your trial by which You send astray whom You will and guide whom You will. You are our Protector, so forgive us and have mercy upon us; and You are the best of forgivers

7:156.ar: ۞وَٱكۡتُبۡ لَنَا فِي هَٰذِهِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا حَسَنَةࣰ وَفِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ إِنَّا هُدۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَۚ قَالَ عَذَابِيٓ أُصِيبُ بِهِۦ مَنۡ أَشَآءُۖ وَرَحۡمَتِي وَسِعَتۡ كُلَّ شَيۡءࣲۚ فَسَأَكۡتُبُهَا لِلَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَ وَيُؤۡتُونَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱلَّذِينَ هُم بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
7:156.en: And decree for us in this world [that which is] good and [also] in the Hereafter; indeed, we have turned back to You." [Allah] said, "My punishment - I afflict with it whom I will, but My mercy encompasses all things." So I will decree it [especially] for those who fear Me and give zakah and those who believe in Our verses

7:157.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ ٱلرَّسُولَ ٱلنَّبِيَّ ٱلۡأُمِّيَّ ٱلَّذِي يَجِدُونَهُۥ مَكۡتُوبًا عِندَهُمۡ فِي ٱلتَّوۡرَىٰةِ وَٱلۡإِنجِيلِ يَأۡمُرُهُم بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِ وَيَنۡهَىٰهُمۡ عَنِ ٱلۡمُنكَرِ وَيُحِلُّ لَهُمُ ٱلطَّيِّبَٰتِ وَيُحَرِّمُ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡخَبَٰٓئِثَ وَيَضَعُ عَنۡهُمۡ إِصۡرَهُمۡ وَٱلۡأَغۡلَٰلَ ٱلَّتِي كَانَتۡ عَلَيۡهِمۡۚ فَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ بِهِۦ وَعَزَّرُوهُ وَنَصَرُوهُ وَٱتَّبَعُواْ ٱلنُّورَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أُنزِلَ مَعَهُۥٓ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ
7:157.en: Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered prophet, whom they find written in what they have of the Torah and the Gospel, who enjoins upon them what is right and forbids them what is wrong and makes lawful for them the good things and prohibits for them the evil and relieves them of their burden and the shackles which were upon them. So they who have believed in him, honored him, supported him and followed the light which was sent down with him - it is those who will be the successful

7:159.ar: وَمِن قَوۡمِ مُوسَىٰٓ أُمَّةࣱ يَهۡدُونَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَبِهِۦ يَعۡدِلُونَ
7:159.en: And among the people of Moses is a community which guides by truth and by it establishes justice

7:160.ar: وَقَطَّعۡنَٰهُمُ ٱثۡنَتَيۡ عَشۡرَةَ أَسۡبَاطًا أُمَمࣰ اۚ وَأَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰٓ إِذِ ٱسۡتَسۡقَىٰهُ قَوۡمُهُۥٓ أَنِ ٱضۡرِب بِّعَصَاكَ ٱلۡحَجَرَۖ فَٱنۢبَجَسَتۡ مِنۡهُ ٱثۡنَتَا عَشۡرَةَ عَيۡنࣰ اۖ قَدۡ عَلِمَ كُلُّ أُنَاسࣲ مَّشۡرَبَهُمۡۚ وَظَلَّلۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡغَمَٰمَ وَأَنزَلۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡمَنَّ وَٱلسَّلۡوَىٰۖ كُلُواْ مِن طَيِّبَٰتِ مَا رَزَقۡنَٰكُمۡۚ وَمَا ظَلَمُونَا وَلَٰكِن كَانُوٓاْ أَنفُسَهُمۡ يَظۡلِمُونَ
7:160.en: And We divided them into twelve descendant tribes [as distinct] nations. And We inspired to Moses when his people implored him for water, "Strike with your staff the stone," and there gushed forth from it twelve springs. Every people knew its watering place. And We shaded them with clouds and sent down upon them manna and quails, [saying], "Eat from the good things with which We have provided you." And they wronged Us not, but they were [only] wronging themselves

7:161.ar: وَإِذۡ قِيلَ لَهُمُ ٱسۡكُنُواْ هَٰذِهِ ٱلۡقَرۡيَةَ وَكُلُواْ مِنۡهَا حَيۡثُ شِئۡتُمۡ وَقُولُواْ حِطَّةࣱ وَٱدۡخُلُواْ ٱلۡبَابَ سُجَّدࣰ ا نَّغۡفِرۡ لَكُمۡ خَطِيٓـَٰٔتِكُمۡۚ سَنَزِيدُ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
7:161.en: And [mention, O Muhammad], when it was said to them, "Dwell in this city and eat from it wherever you will and say, 'Relieve us of our burdens,' and enter the gate bowing humbly; We will [then] forgive you your sins. We will increase the doers of good [in goodness and reward]

7:162.ar: فَبَدَّلَ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ مِنۡهُمۡ قَوۡلًا غَيۡرَ ٱلَّذِي قِيلَ لَهُمۡ فَأَرۡسَلۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ رِجۡزࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ بِمَا كَانُواْ يَظۡلِمُونَ
7:162.en: But those who wronged among them changed [the words] to a statement other than that which had been said to them. So We sent upon them a punishment from the sky for the wrong that they were doing

7:163.ar: وَسۡـَٔلۡهُمۡ عَنِ ٱلۡقَرۡيَةِ ٱلَّتِي كَانَتۡ حَاضِرَةَ ٱلۡبَحۡرِ إِذۡ يَعۡدُونَ فِي ٱلسَّبۡتِ إِذۡ تَأۡتِيهِمۡ حِيتَانُهُمۡ يَوۡمَ سَبۡتِهِمۡ شُرَّعࣰ ا وَيَوۡمَ لَا يَسۡبِتُونَ لَا تَأۡتِيهِمۡۚ كَذَٰلِكَ نَبۡلُوهُم بِمَا كَانُواْ يَفۡسُقُونَ
7:163.en: And ask them about the town that was by the sea - when they transgressed in [the matter of] the sabbath - when their fish came to them openly on their sabbath day, and the day they had no sabbath they did not come to them. Thus did We give them trial because they were defiantly disobedient

7:164.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَتۡ أُمَّةࣱ مِّنۡهُمۡ لِمَ تَعِظُونَ قَوۡمًا ٱللَّهُ مُهۡلِكُهُمۡ أَوۡ مُعَذِّبُهُمۡ عَذَابࣰ ا شَدِيدࣰ اۖ قَالُواْ مَعۡذِرَةً إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُمۡ وَلَعَلَّهُمۡ يَتَّقُونَ
7:164.en: And when a community among them said, "Why do you advise [or warn] a people whom Allah is [about] to destroy or to punish with a severe punishment?" they [the advisors] said, "To be absolved before your Lord and perhaps they may fear Him

7:165.ar: فَلَمَّا نَسُواْ مَا ذُكِّرُواْ بِهِۦٓ أَنجَيۡنَا ٱلَّذِينَ يَنۡهَوۡنَ عَنِ ٱلسُّوٓءِ وَأَخَذۡنَا ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ بِعَذَابِۭ بَـِٔيسِۭ بِمَا كَانُواْ يَفۡسُقُونَ
7:165.en: And when they forgot that by which they had been reminded, We saved those who had forbidden evil and seized those who wronged, with a wretched punishment, because they were defiantly disobeying

7:166.ar: فَلَمَّا عَتَوۡاْ عَن مَّا نُهُواْ عَنۡهُ قُلۡنَا لَهُمۡ كُونُواْ قِرَدَةً خَٰسِـِٔينَ
7:166.en: So when they were insolent about that which they had been forbidden, We said to them, "Be apes, despised

7:168.ar: وَقَطَّعۡنَٰهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ أُمَمࣰ اۖ مِّنۡهُمُ ٱلصَّٰلِحُونَ وَمِنۡهُمۡ دُونَ ذَٰلِكَۖ وَبَلَوۡنَٰهُم بِٱلۡحَسَنَٰتِ وَٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَرۡجِعُونَ
7:168.en: And We divided them throughout the earth into nations. Of them some were righteous, and of them some were otherwise. And We tested them with good [times] and bad that perhaps they would return [to obedience]

7:172.ar: وَإِذۡ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِنۢ بَنِيٓ ءَادَمَ مِن ظُهُورِهِمۡ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمۡ وَأَشۡهَدَهُمۡ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ أَلَسۡتُ بِرَبِّكُمۡۖ قَالُواْ بَلَىٰ شَهِدۡنَآۚ أَن تَقُولُواْ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ إِنَّا كُنَّا عَنۡ هَٰذَا غَٰفِلِينَ
7:172.en: And [mention] when your Lord took from the children of Adam - from their loins - their descendants and made them testify of themselves, [saying to them], "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we have testified." [This] - lest you should say on the day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were of this unaware

7:173.ar: أَوۡ تَقُولُوٓاْ إِنَّمَآ أَشۡرَكَ ءَابَآؤُنَا مِن قَبۡلُ وَكُنَّا ذُرِّيَّةࣰ مِّنۢ بَعۡدِهِمۡۖ أَفَتُهۡلِكُنَا بِمَا فَعَلَ ٱلۡمُبۡطِلُونَ
7:173.en: Or [lest] you say, "It was only that our fathers associated [others in worship] with Allah before, and we were but descendants after them. Then would You destroy us for what the falsifiers have done

7:175.ar: وَٱتۡلُ عَلَيۡهِمۡ نَبَأَ ٱلَّذِيٓ ءَاتَيۡنَٰهُ ءَايَٰتِنَا فَٱنسَلَخَ مِنۡهَا فَأَتۡبَعَهُ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ فَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡغَاوِينَ
7:175.en: And recite to them, [O Muhammad], the news of him to whom we gave [knowledge of] Our signs, but he detached himself from them; so Satan pursued him, and he became of the deviators

7:176.ar: وَلَوۡ شِئۡنَا لَرَفَعۡنَٰهُ بِهَا وَلَٰكِنَّهُۥٓ أَخۡلَدَ إِلَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَٱتَّبَعَ هَوَىٰهُۚ فَمَثَلُهُۥ كَمَثَلِ ٱلۡكَلۡبِ إِن تَحۡمِلۡ عَلَيۡهِ يَلۡهَثۡ أَوۡ تَتۡرُكۡهُ يَلۡهَثۚ ذَّٰلِكَ مَثَلُ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَاۚ فَٱقۡصُصِ ٱلۡقَصَصَ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
7:176.en: And if We had willed, we could have elevated him thereby, but he adhered [instead] to the earth and followed his own desire. So his example is like that of the dog: if you chase him, he pants, or if you leave him, he [still] pants. That is the example of the people who denied Our signs. So relate the stories that perhaps they will give thought

7:177.ar: سَآءَ مَثَلًا ٱلۡقَوۡمُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا وَأَنفُسَهُمۡ كَانُواْ يَظۡلِمُونَ
7:177.en: How evil an example [is that of] the people who denied Our signs and used to wrong themselves

7:178.ar: مَن يَهۡدِ ٱللَّهُ فَهُوَ ٱلۡمُهۡتَدِيۖ وَمَن يُضۡلِلۡ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡخَٰسِرُونَ
7:178.en: Whoever Allah guides - he is the [rightly] guided; and whoever He sends astray - it is those who are the losers

7:180.ar: وَلِلَّهِ ٱلۡأَسۡمَآءُ ٱلۡحُسۡنَىٰ فَٱدۡعُوهُ بِهَاۖ وَذَرُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ يُلۡحِدُونَ فِيٓ أَسۡمَٰٓئِهِۦۚ سَيُجۡزَوۡنَ مَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
7:180.en: And to Allah belong the best names, so invoke Him by them. And leave [the company of] those who practice deviation concerning His names. They will be recompensed for what they have been doing

7:187.ar: يَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلسَّاعَةِ أَيَّانَ مُرۡسَىٰهَاۖ قُلۡ إِنَّمَا عِلۡمُهَا عِندَ رَبِّيۖ لَا يُجَلِّيهَا لِوَقۡتِهَآ إِلَّا هُوَۚ ثَقُلَتۡ فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ لَا تَأۡتِيكُمۡ إِلَّا بَغۡتَةࣰۗ يَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ كَأَنَّكَ حَفِيٌّ عَنۡهَاۖ قُلۡ إِنَّمَا عِلۡمُهَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
7:187.en: They ask you, [O Muhammad], about the Hour: when is its arrival? Say, "Its knowledge is only with my Lord. None will reveal its time except Him. It lays heavily upon the heavens and the earth. It will not come upon you except unexpectedly." They ask you as if you are familiar with it. Say, "Its knowledge is only with Allah, but most of the people do not know

7:188.ar: قُل لَّآ أَمۡلِكُ لِنَفۡسِي نَفۡعࣰ ا وَلَا ضَرًّا إِلَّا مَا شَآءَ ٱللَّهُۚ وَلَوۡ كُنتُ أَعۡلَمُ ٱلۡغَيۡبَ لَٱسۡتَكۡثَرۡتُ مِنَ ٱلۡخَيۡرِ وَمَا مَسَّنِيَ ٱلسُّوٓءُۚ إِنۡ أَنَا۠ إِلَّا نَذِيرࣱ وَبَشِيرࣱ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يُؤۡمِنُونَ
7:188.en: Say, "I hold not for myself [the power of] benefit or harm, except what Allah has willed. And if I knew the unseen, I could have acquired much wealth, and no harm would have touched me. I am not except a warner and a bringer of good tidings to a people who believe

7:196.ar: إِنَّ وَلِـِّۧيَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي نَزَّلَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَۖ وَهُوَ يَتَوَلَّى ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
7:196.en: Indeed, my protector is Allah, who has sent down the Book; and He is an ally to the righteous

7:197.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ تَدۡعُونَ مِن دُونِهِۦ لَا يَسۡتَطِيعُونَ نَصۡرَكُمۡ وَلَآ أَنفُسَهُمۡ يَنصُرُونَ
7:197.en: And those you call upon besides Him are unable to help you, nor can they help themselves

7:199.ar: خُذِ ٱلۡعَفۡوَ وَأۡمُرۡ بِٱلۡعُرۡفِ وَأَعۡرِضۡ عَنِ ٱلۡجَٰهِلِينَ
7:199.en: Take what is given freely, enjoin what is good, and turn away from the ignorant

7:200.ar: وَإِمَّا يَنزَغَنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِ نَزۡغࣱ فَٱسۡتَعِذۡ بِٱللَّهِۚ إِنَّهُۥ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ
7:200.en: And if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is Hearing and Knowing

7:201.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوۡاْ إِذَا مَسَّهُمۡ طَٰٓئِفࣱ مِّنَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِ تَذَكَّرُواْ فَإِذَا هُم مُّبۡصِرُونَ
7:201.en: Indeed, those who fear Allah - when an impulse touches them from Satan, they remember [Him] and at once they have insight

7:204.ar: وَإِذَا قُرِئَ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانُ فَٱسۡتَمِعُواْ لَهُۥ وَأَنصِتُواْ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تُرۡحَمُونَ
7:204.en: So when the Qur'an is recited, then listen to it and pay attention that you may receive mercy

7:205.ar: وَٱذۡكُر رَّبَّكَ فِي نَفۡسِكَ تَضَرُّعࣰ ا وَخِيفَةࣰ وَدُونَ ٱلۡجَهۡرِ مِنَ ٱلۡقَوۡلِ بِٱلۡغُدُوِّ وَٱلۡأٓصَالِ وَلَا تَكُن مِّنَ ٱلۡغَٰفِلِينَ
7:205.en: And remember your Lord within yourself in humility and in fear without being apparent in speech - in the mornings and the evenings. And do not be among the heedless

7:206.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ عِندَ رَبِّكَ لَا يَسۡتَكۡبِرُونَ عَنۡ عِبَادَتِهِۦ وَيُسَبِّحُونَهُۥ وَلَهُۥ يَسۡجُدُونَۤ۩
7:206.en: Indeed, those who are near your Lord are not prevented by arrogance from His worship, and they exalt Him, and to Him they prostrate

3:152.ar: وَلَقَدۡ صَدَقَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَعۡدَهُۥٓ إِذۡ تَحُسُّونَهُم بِإِذۡنِهِۦۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا فَشِلۡتُمۡ وَتَنَٰزَعۡتُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَمۡرِ وَعَصَيۡتُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ مَآ أَرَىٰكُم مَّا تُحِبُّونَۚ مِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةَۚ ثُمَّ صَرَفَكُمۡ عَنۡهُمۡ لِيَبۡتَلِيَكُمۡۖ وَلَقَدۡ عَفَا عَنكُمۡۗ وَٱللَّهُ ذُو فَضۡلٍ عَلَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
3:152.en: And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing the enemy by His permission until [the time] when you lost courage and fell to disputing about the order [given by the Prophet] and disobeyed after He had shown you that which you love. Among you are some who desire this world, and among you are some who desire the Hereafter. Then he turned you back from them [defeated] that He might test you. And He has already forgiven you, and Allah is the possessor of bounty for the believers

6:103.ar: لَّا تُدۡرِكُهُ ٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرُ وَهُوَ يُدۡرِكُ ٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرَۖ وَهُوَ ٱللَّطِيفُ ٱلۡخَبِيرُ
6:103.en: Vision perceives Him not, but He perceives [all] vision; and He is the Subtle, the Acquainted

14:48.ar: يَوۡمَ تُبَدَّلُ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ غَيۡرَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُۖ وَبَرَزُواْ لِلَّهِ ٱلۡوَٰحِدِ ٱلۡقَهَّارِ
14:48.en: [It will be] on the Day the earth will be replaced by another earth, and the heavens [as well], and all creatures will come out before Allah, the One, the Prevailing

ArZAqC5ylbU.speaker: adnan
ArZAqC5ylbU.speaker_note: hosts his own A Juz A Day Ramadan series; single voice throughout
ArZAqC5ylbU.title: A Juz A Day: 9th Juz, Musa vs Pharaoh
ArZAqC5ylbU.one_line: Surah Al-A'raf from Shuayb to the end: Musa against Pharaoh, the Israelites' lapses, the Sabbath-breakers and their preachers, and the primordial covenant.
ArZAqC5ylbU.summary: He reads the ninth juz as the second half of Surah Al-A'raf. Shuayb begins with tawhid but also confronts his people's financial corruption, which shows that believers must lead on society's moral problems, and calling him their brother shows that dawah starts from shared humanity, a lesson for Muslims in a non-Muslim country. Allah sends hardship to break arrogance, and those who stay arrogant are given prosperity before a harsher punishment; breaking commitments marks the evil. In the Musa narrative, the sorcerers recognize a real miracle and fall into prostration, holding firm under Pharaoh's threats, an example of courage born of iman and help from unexpected places. Pharaoh's people break their promise after every plague. He notes that the Quran praises the Israelites when they are patient and criticizes even the Companions when they err, a balance critics ignore. He discusses Musa's request to see Allah out of love, the calf, accountability starting at the top, and Allah's mercy that keeps offering chances. The Sabbath preachers model all advocacy: speak so you are excused before Allah and because someone may listen. The covenant of souls grounds the fitrah, and disbelief is its suppression. He closes with dua by Allah's names, forgiveness, commanding good and remembering Allah.

outline.heading: Opening
Shuayb's call to Midian
outline.gist: Worship Allah alone, give full measure, do not cheat people or spread corruption, and do not block the path of believers.

outline.heading: Threatened with expulsion, Shuayb refuses to return
outline.gist: Returning to their religion after Allah saved them would make them liars about their faith and about their principles; they put their trust in Allah and ask Him to judge.

outline.heading: The earthquake and Shuayb's farewell
outline.gist: The deniers are destroyed as if they never lived there, and Shuayb turns away having delivered his message and sincere advice.

outline.heading: Faith must address society's moral problems
outline.gist: Shuayb's people were financially exploitative; prophets addressed the specific moral rot of their society, and believers should lead on any oppression or unethical practice that affects everyone.

outline.heading: 'Their brother': dawah from shared humanity
outline.gist: Each prophet is called the brother of his people; dawah should start from shared identity and humanity rather than hostility, especially for Muslims in a non-Muslim majority country.

outline.heading: Hardship to humble, then prosperity before ruin
outline.gist: Before destroying a nation Allah sent hardship to break its arrogance; those who stayed arrogant were given prosperity, and their punishment then was fully deserved, a warning to Quraysh.

outline.heading: Do they feel safe from Allah's plan?
outline.gist: Had they believed they would have received blessings; the warnings about punishment by night or at play are meant to make us reprioritize, since individuals can still be punished to bring them back.

outline.heading: Most of them did not honour their commitments
outline.gist: Keeping promises separates good from evil people; someone who cannot be trusted with a promise cannot be trusted with iman and salvation.

outline.heading: Musa before Pharaoh: the staff and the hand
outline.gist: Musa declares his message and asks for the Israelites' release, showing the staff turning to a snake and his hand shining white.

outline.heading: Pharaoh gathers the sorcerers
outline.gist: The court calls Musa a sorcerer; the best magicians are summoned and ask for a reward; their spell petrifies the crowd and Musa feels natural fear.

outline.heading: The staff devours their tricks and the sorcerers fall prostrate
outline.gist: Experts in illusion recognize a real miracle and are thrown into prostration, believing in the Lord of Musa and Harun.

outline.heading: Pharaoh's threat and the sorcerers' steadfastness
outline.gist: Pharaoh brands them a national security threat and threatens crucifixion; they answer that their only crime is belief and ask Allah for patience and to die as Muslims.

outline.heading: Help from unexpected places and the courage of iman
outline.gist: Allah sends a prophet helpers from among his enemies, as He kept sending help to the Prophet in Makkah; courage that ignores consequences validates iman.

outline.heading: The earth belongs to Allah; the end belongs to the righteous
outline.gist: Rule of the earth is not a sign of goodness; Allah gives it as He wills, but the Hereafter is exclusively for the righteous, so seek help and stay steadfast.

outline.heading: Do not give up hope
outline.gist: The Israelites complain they are always persecuted; Musa tells them Allah may make them successors to see how they act.

outline.heading: Drought and plagues met with arrogance
outline.gist: Pharaoh's people credit themselves for good and blame Musa's omen for bad; the flood, locusts, lice, frogs and blood only harden them.

outline.heading: A broken promise after every plague
outline.gist: Each time they beg Musa to pray for relief and promise to release the Israelites, then break the pledge, showing they are people of no principle.

outline.heading: Pharaoh drowned, the oppressed inherit the land
outline.gist: The brutally oppressed are made to rule the blessed land, east and west.

outline.heading: The Quran's balance: praise where due, blame where due
outline.gist: Allah credits the Israelites' patience and blames the Companions' mistakes at Uhud explicitly; critics who call the Quran hateful ignore this balance.

outline.heading: 'Make us a god like theirs'
outline.gist: Freshly saved from Pharaoh, the Israelites ask for an idol; Musa calls them foolish and reminds them of Allah's favour.

outline.heading: The forty nights and Harun as deputy
outline.gist: Musa's appointment grows from thirty to forty nights, and he leaves Harun in charge with instructions to keep order.

outline.heading: Musa asks to see Allah out of love
outline.gist: The request came not from doubt but from love and longing in one whom Allah spoke to directly.

outline.heading: The mountain crumbles; believers will see Allah later
outline.gist: No one can bear seeing Allah in this world; a glimpse turned a mountain to dust, but in the Hereafter, when the laws of this world end, the believers will see their Lord.

outline.heading: Musa repents and is reassured
outline.gist: Recognizing the request was not ideal, Musa repents at once; Allah reassures him he is chosen and tells him to hold firm and be grateful.

outline.heading: The tablets
outline.gist: Musa receives the tablets explaining everything, the revelation for his people.

outline.heading: The lowing calf that cannot guide
outline.gist: In his absence they worship a calf of jewellery that only makes a sound; idols cannot speak or guide, while Allah guides through revelation, reason and inspiration of the heart.

outline.heading: Musa's anger: accountability starts at the top
outline.gist: He seizes Harun, the one in charge, first; Harun explains they nearly killed him, and Musa prays for forgiveness for both.

outline.heading: The calf-worshippers' repentance and our easier tawbah
outline.gist: Their repentance required their lives because the stakes were so high; ours is words, resolve and remorse.

outline.heading: Guidance and mercy on the tablets; the seventy
outline.gist: All revelation carries guidance and mercy; the chosen seventy ask for something egregious, are punished and revived.

outline.heading: My mercy encompasses all things
outline.gist: Despite repeated failures the Israelites kept receiving prophets and chances; Allah keeps giving us chances and sends difficulty to humble us back to Him.

outline.heading: The unlettered Prophet who lifts burdens
outline.gist: He is described in the Torah and Gospel as bringing an easy law that removes the shackles of a hard one.

outline.heading: Not all alike: the twelve springs, cloud shade, manna and quails
outline.gist: The Quran praises a righteous group among them and recounts how Allah provided for the twelve tribes; when they complained, they wronged only themselves.

outline.heading: The Sabbath-breakers' loophole
outline.gist: Fish came only on the Sabbath, so they set rigs on Friday and collected on Sunday, trying to cut corners without openly breaking the law.

outline.heading: Why the preachers kept preaching
outline.gist: Told they were wasting their time, the preachers answered: to be excused before Allah, and because someone might listen; those who forbade evil were saved.

outline.heading: The basis of all activism and advocacy
outline.gist: Writing to MPs or speaking up is done so we can say we tried and because pressure can work; stay proactive and leave results to Allah.

outline.heading: Dispersed and tested with good and bad
outline.gist: The Israelites were scattered, some righteous, and tested with blessings and misfortune so they would return.

outline.heading: The covenant: 'Am I not your Lord?'
outline.gist: Allah drew out the offspring of Adam and made them testify, removing the excuse of blaming forefathers on Judgment Day.

outline.heading: The soul's pledge as the root of fitrah and morality
outline.gist: Souls existed before bodies and all took the pledge; its remnant drives the search for purpose and is the basis of ethics.

outline.heading: Kufr as suppression of the fitrah
outline.gist: Living without purpose requires suppressing the innate search for Allah; that suppression is disbelief, and every sane adult is accountable to their fitrah, with Allah judging what message reached them.

outline.heading: The man who cast off the signs: salvation is not guaranteed
outline.gist: Being born Muslim does not make salvation a done deal; it must be worked for every day.

outline.heading: Call on Allah by His beautiful names
outline.gist: Match the name to the need in dua: the Powerful for strength, the Provider for provision, the Forgiving for forgiveness, the Bestower for a child.

outline.heading: The Hour and the Prophet's human role
outline.gist: Only Allah knows the Hour; the Prophet has no power over benefit or harm and no knowledge of the unseen except what Allah grants; he is a warner and bearer of good news.

outline.heading: Only Allah protects
outline.gist: Those called on besides Him cannot even help themselves, so dua and worship are for Allah alone.

outline.heading: Forgive, command the good, turn from the ignorant
outline.gist: Three pillars of Islamic ethics: habitual pardoning and gentleness, working for justice in society, and knowledge that lets you stay gracious with provocateurs.

outline.heading: When Satan prompts, remember and see clearly
outline.gist: Believers slip, but the mindful remember Allah at once, seek forgiveness and set things right.

outline.heading: Listen to the Quran and remember Allah morning and evening
outline.gist: Quiet, humble, private remembrance as the Prophet practised it reconnects us when we stray.

outline.heading: The first prostration of the Quran
outline.gist: Those near Allah are not too proud to worship Him; the surah ends with the first sajdah in the mushaf.

outline.heading: Outro

The earth and skies will be changed, so the limits that prevent seeing Allah end in the Hereafter

Accountability is top down
So we can tell Allah we did something, and maybe someone listens

36:3.en: Indeed you, [O Muhammad], are from among the messengers

36:5.en: [This is] a revelation of the Exalted in Might, the Merciful

36:6.ar: لِتُنذِرَ قَوۡمࣰ ا مَّآ أُنذِرَ ءَابَآؤُهُمۡ فَهُمۡ غَٰفِلُونَ
36:6.en: That you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned, so they are unaware

36:7.ar: لَقَدۡ حَقَّ ٱلۡقَوۡلُ عَلَىٰٓ أَكۡثَرِهِمۡ فَهُمۡ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
36:7.en: Already the word has come into effect upon most of them, so they do not believe

36:8.ar: إِنَّا جَعَلۡنَا فِيٓ أَعۡنَٰقِهِمۡ أَغۡلَٰلࣰ ا فَهِيَ إِلَى ٱلۡأَذۡقَانِ فَهُم مُّقۡمَحُونَ
36:8.en: Indeed, We have put shackles on their necks, and they are to their chins, so they are with heads [kept] aloft

36:9.ar: وَجَعَلۡنَا مِنۢ بَيۡنِ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ سَدࣰّ ا وَمِنۡ خَلۡفِهِمۡ سَدࣰّ ا فَأَغۡشَيۡنَٰهُمۡ فَهُمۡ لَا يُبۡصِرُونَ
36:9.en: And We have put before them a barrier and behind them a barrier and covered them, so they do not see

36:10.ar: وَسَوَآءٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَأَنذَرۡتَهُمۡ أَمۡ لَمۡ تُنذِرۡهُمۡ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
36:10.en: And it is all the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them - they will not believe

36:11.ar: إِنَّمَا تُنذِرُ مَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ ٱلذِّكۡرَ وَخَشِيَ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنَ بِٱلۡغَيۡبِۖ فَبَشِّرۡهُ بِمَغۡفِرَةࣲ وَأَجۡرࣲ كَرِيمٍ
36:11.en: You can only warn one who follows the message and fears the Most Merciful unseen. So give him good tidings of forgiveness and noble reward

36:12.ar: إِنَّا نَحۡنُ نُحۡيِ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰ وَنَكۡتُبُ مَا قَدَّمُواْ وَءَاثَٰرَهُمۡۚ وَكُلَّ شَيۡءٍ أَحۡصَيۡنَٰهُ فِيٓ إِمَامࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
36:12.en: Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life and record what they have put forth and what they left behind, and all things We have enumerated in a clear register

36:13.ar: وَٱضۡرِبۡ لَهُم مَّثَلًا أَصۡحَٰبَ ٱلۡقَرۡيَةِ إِذۡ جَآءَهَا ٱلۡمُرۡسَلُونَ
36:13.en: And present to them an example: the people of the city, when the messengers came to it

36:14.ar: إِذۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَآ إِلَيۡهِمُ ٱثۡنَيۡنِ فَكَذَّبُوهُمَا فَعَزَّزۡنَا بِثَالِثࣲ فَقَالُوٓاْ إِنَّآ إِلَيۡكُم مُّرۡسَلُونَ
36:14.en: When We sent to them two but they denied them, so We strengthened them with a third, and they said, "Indeed, we are messengers to you

36:15.ar: قَالُواْ مَآ أَنتُمۡ إِلَّا بَشَرࣱ مِّثۡلُنَا وَمَآ أَنزَلَ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ مِن شَيۡءٍ إِنۡ أَنتُمۡ إِلَّا تَكۡذِبُونَ
36:15.en: They said, "You are not but human beings like us, and the Most Merciful has not revealed a thing. You are only telling lies

36:16.ar: قَالُواْ رَبُّنَا يَعۡلَمُ إِنَّآ إِلَيۡكُمۡ لَمُرۡسَلُونَ
36:16.en: They said, "Our Lord knows that we are messengers to you

36:17.en: And we are not responsible except for clear notification

36:18.ar: قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا تَطَيَّرۡنَا بِكُمۡۖ لَئِن لَّمۡ تَنتَهُواْ لَنَرۡجُمَنَّكُمۡ وَلَيَمَسَّنَّكُم مِّنَّا عَذَابٌ أَلِيمࣱ‏
36:18.en: They said, "Indeed, we consider you a bad omen. If you do not desist, we will surely stone you, and there will surely touch you, from us, a painful punishment

36:19.ar: قَالُواْ طَٰٓئِرُكُم مَّعَكُمۡ أَئِن ذُكِّرۡتُمۚ بَلۡ أَنتُمۡ قَوۡمࣱ مُّسۡرِفُونَ
36:19.en: They said, "Your omen is with yourselves. Is it because you were reminded? Rather, you are a transgressing people

2:124.ar: ۞وَإِذِ ٱبۡتَلَىٰٓ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمَ رَبُّهُۥ بِكَلِمَٰتࣲ فَأَتَمَّهُنَّۖ قَالَ إِنِّي جَاعِلُكَ لِلنَّاسِ إِمَامࣰ اۖ قَالَ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِيۖ قَالَ لَا يَنَالُ عَهۡدِي ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
2:124.en: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Abraham was tried by his Lord with commands and he fulfilled them. [Allah] said, "Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people." [Abraham] said, "And of my descendants?" [Allah] said, "My covenant does not include the wrongdoers

79:18.ar: فَقُلۡ هَل لَّكَ إِلَىٰٓ أَن تَزَكَّىٰ
79:18.en: And say to him, 'Would you [be willing to] purify yourself
